Dear colleagues,

I attach a PhD opportunity on behalf of Antonio Hernández-Matías, from the University of Barcelona. The candidate needs to have a completed BSc. in Biology, Environmental Sciences, Ecology, or a related discipline, plus a master's degree. This opportunity is not funded yet, but the selected candidate will apply for a grant from the Spanish Research Ministry (FPU). A summary follows below, and more information can be found in the attached file.

Raptors under human pressure: agricultural intensification, energy infrastructure and conservation across spatial scales

Birds of prey are sensitive indicators of environmental change, and many
populations face two major pressures: agricultural intensification and the rapid
expansion of energy infrastructure. How do these pressures affect raptor
distribution, abundance and population trends? Do these effects vary across
Catalonia, Spain and Europe? And what do the findings mean for biodiversity
conservation and territorial planning, including decisions on energy development?

This PhD will examine how agricultural intensification and energy infrastructure
shape the distribution, abundance and population trends of raptors at three spatial
scales: Catalonia, Spain and Europe. The research will be developed within
RAPTORCONS, a research project funded by the Spanish State Research Agency
(Agencia Estatal de Investigación, AEI). You will work with large datasets from bird
atlases, long-term monitoring programmes and citizen science platforms, using
advanced statistical approaches to address challenges associated with
observational data, including differences in sampling effort and observation
processes

All the best,

Jaume A. Badia-Boher
